open_points.subject: A6 record validation
open_points.text: A placement or mark record that exists but cannot be read, is not valid JSON, is not an object or lacks a field of its model is never taken for an absent record
open_points.question: What happens when an existing object has every required field but a field has the wrong type, an invalid enum value, a malformed nested model, null where the model disallows it, or an unknown extra field?
options: Refuse the operation with state_unavailable and change nothing
Accept any object containing all required field names
Validate types and nested values but ignore unknown extra fields
open_points.default_guess: Validate the complete model, ignore harmless extra fields, and refuse every other validation failure with state_unavailable without changing state.

witness.initial: A placement JSON object contains every M04 field, but size is a string instead of an integer.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The scan refuses with state_unavailable and leaves the record untouched.
The scan accepts the record because no field is absent and reports the placement.

open_points.subject: A6 nested record fields
open_points.text: lacks a field of its model
open_points.question: Does “its model” include every field of nested models such as M04.publication, or only the top-level placement or mark fields?
options: Validate all nested model fields recursively
Check only top-level fields
Validate only fields the current operation reads
open_points.default_guess: Validate all nested model fields recursively.

witness.initial: An M04 record has a publication object with no photo_date field.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The scan refuses with state_unavailable because a nested model field is absent.
The scan accepts the placement because every top-level M04 field exists.

open_points.subject: A6 lock-file creation
open_points.text: The same refusal answers a failure to open or lock the lock file
open_points.question: Is a project lock file created on first use when it does not exist, or is its absence an open failure that must return state_unavailable?
options: Create the missing lock file atomically and then lock it
Require the lock file to have been provisioned and refuse when it is absent
open_points.default_guess: Create the missing lock file in the state folder with a fixed safe mode, then acquire its operating-system lock.

witness.initial: A valid confirmed project has no lock file because no delivery or mark has run before.
events: The calling flow requests the first delivery.
outcomes: The service creates and locks the file, then performs the delivery.
The service refuses with state_unavailable because opening the absent file failed.

open_points.subject: A6 project lock
open_points.text: one lock file of that project in the state folder
open_points.question: What exact name and path derive the per-project lock file, and how is it guaranteed that distinct project identifiers cannot collide or escape the state folder?
options: Use a specified canonical project-id filename directly under the state folder
Use a specified digest of the canonical project id
Leave the backend to choose any collision-free mapping
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical UUID text plus a fixed .lock suffix directly under the state folder and reject any noncanonical project identifier before path construction.

open_points.subject: A6 lock errors
open_points.text: a failure to open or lock the lock file, which waiting for another holder is not
open_points.question: Which operating-system results are retryable waiting or interruption, and which are final failures returning state_unavailable?
options: Retry contention and interrupted system calls indefinitely; refuse other errors
Retry only contention and refuse interrupted calls
Treat cancellation or process shutdown as a distinct transport-level termination
open_points.default_guess: Retry contention and EINTR, allow process cancellation to terminate the request, and return state_unavailable for other open or lock errors.

open_points.subject: A6 mark write atomicity
open_points.text: Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none. Atomicity is per file. A mark that cannot be written is refused with `state_unavailable` and changes nothing.
open_points.question: If the mark has already been renamed into place but synchronising its folder fails, is the mark considered written, must it be rolled back, or may the call refuse despite the visible state change?
options: Treat rename as the commit and return success despite the later directory-sync failure
Remove or restore the mark and return state_unavailable
Return state_unavailable while leaving the complete mark visible
open_points.default_guess: Treat the rename as commit for observable state and report success if the resulting mark can be read back; separately surface durability failure operationally.

witness.initial: No publication mark exists, and the temporary mark can be written and synchronised.
events: The service renames the temporary mark into its final name.
outcomes: The call refuses with state_unavailable although a new mark is now visible, contradicting “changes nothing.”
The call reports marked because the mark became visible, despite failure to complete the stated write protocol.
witness.observer: The calling flow on this call and on a later scan

open_points.subject: A6 placement write failures
open_points.text: The same refusal answers a failure to open or lock the lock file, which waiting for another holder is not, and a mark that cannot be written.
open_points.question: What outcome and rollback are required when the prepared image or placement record, rather than a mark, cannot be written, synchronised, renamed, or followed by folder synchronisation?
options: Refuse the whole operation with state_unavailable and leave no image or placement
Return an M06 failed outcome
Keep any completed file and allow a later call to repair the placement
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with state_unavailable and remove any newly visible image or placement so the operation leaves no new placement state.

witness.initial: No placement exists and the binary-store image can be written, but writing the placement record fails because the state filesystem is full.
events: The calling flow requests delivery of a valid ready source.
outcomes: The service returns an M08 state_unavailable refusal and removes the new image.
The service returns an M06 failure or leaves the image for a later retry because only an unwritable mark is assigned state_unavailable.
witness.observer: The calling flow and an operator inspecting the binary store

open_points.subject: A6 unsafe values in state records
open_points.text: The reference must stay inside the binary store. A placement or mark record that exists but cannot be read, is not valid JSON, is not an object or lacks a field of its model is never taken for an absent record
open_points.question: When a syntactically complete record contains an unsafe file_ref or another value that violates its model's semantic constraints, is the result state_unavailable, unsafe_reference, or another outcome?
options: Treat the persisted record as damaged and refuse with state_unavailable
Return unsafe_reference
Accept the record but never dereference the unsafe value
open_points.default_guess: Treat an unsafe value in persisted state as damaged state and refuse with state_unavailable without dereferencing it.

witness.initial: An M04 JSON object has every field, but file_ref resolves outside the binary store.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The scan refuses with state_unavailable because trusted state is corrupt.
The scan refuses with unsafe_reference because the reference is unsafe.

open_points.subject: INV-12 Required tests
open_points.text: concurrent placements of one source answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed`, and marks from separate processes with two `photo_id` values answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other
open_points.question: Must the tests also inspect persistent state and the binary store to show that exactly one placement and one mark were produced, rather than merely checking returned statuses?
options: Assert one final placement record, one stored image, one final mark, and their winning identities
Check only the response statuses named here
open_points.default_guess: Assert both the responses and exactly one final placement, image, and mark with the expected identity.

events: Two processes concurrently deliver the same source.
A faulty implementation writes two physical placement artifacts but returns placed to one caller and replayed to the other.
outcomes: The required test passes because it checks only statuses.
The required test fails because it also asserts that only one placement and stored image exist.
witness.observer: The test suite and an operator inspecting persistent state

open_points.subject: INV-20 Required tests
open_points.text: with a damaged placement or mark record, scan, delivery and mark each answer `state_unavailable` and the record stays as it was
open_points.question: Must this be demonstrated for every damage class listed by rule 5 and for both placement and mark records, or is one representative damaged record sufficient?
options: Exercise unreadable, invalid JSON, non-object, and each missing-field case for both record kinds and applicable operations
Use one representative damaged placement and one representative damaged mark
Use a single damaged-record example
open_points.default_guess: Use parameterized tests covering every listed damage class for both record kinds and every applicable operation.

open_points.subject: M07 marked_at
open_points.question: What authority supplies the instant written to marked_at?
options: An injected system-clock backend decided by State 2
A datetime parameter supplied by the caller
The operating system clock read directly by the persistence code
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected system-clock backend owned by the service, with no direct ambient clock reads.

open_points.subject: M07 marked_at
open_points.question: In what representation is marked_at held in memory and serialized in the publication-mark record?
options: Timezone-aware UTC datetime and a canonical offset-bearing JSON string
Naive UTC datetime and a canonical offset-free JSON string
Integer Unix time at a specified precision
open_points.default_guess: Use a timezone-aware UTC datetime in memory and canonical RFC 3339 UTC text with Z at microsecond precision in storage.

open_points.subject: publication marking operation
open_points.text: The first mark stands when it is sent again, and its `marked_at` does not change
open_points.question: How many time-source readings does one marking operation take, and does a replay or publication conflict read the clock at all?
options: Read exactly once only when creating the first mark
Read once at the start of every mark request but discard it on replay or conflict
Permit any number of readings as long as the stored first timestamp is unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Read exactly once after validation and immediately before creating a new mark; perform no clock read for replay or conflict.

witness.initial: A mark already exists with photo_id A and marked_at T1.
events: The calling flow repeats A while the clock source is unavailable.
outcomes: The request returns replayed without consulting the clock.
The request fails because every mark request reads the clock before discovering the replay.

open_points.subject: M08 Refusal.detail
open_points.text: `detail` is a fixed sentence for people that holds no server path and no credential
open_points.question: What exact fixed sentence corresponds to each RefusalCode, including language, punctuation, and whether any safe request values may be interpolated?
options: Define one exact constant sentence per code with no interpolation
Allow implementations to choose any stable sentence satisfying the secrecy constraint
Return one common sentence for every refusal code
open_points.default_guess: Define one imported constant table mapping every RefusalCode member to an exact non-interpolated English sentence.

witness.initial: A request is refused with unknown_project.
outcomes: The caller receives “Unknown project.”
The caller receives “The requested project is not connected.”
witness.observer: The calling flow and the owner shown its message

open_points.subject: M08 RefusalCode
open_points.question: For each operation, what exact condition selects invalid_source_id, unsafe_reference, and folder_unavailable, and which failures remain an M06 per-photo failure instead?
options: Provide a closed operation-by-condition refusal table
Let each operation choose among semantically similar codes
Define the three codes globally and apply them wherever their predicates hold
open_points.default_guess: Provide a closed table for scan, delivery, and mark, with precise predicates and an explicit boundary between M08 and M06.

open_points.subject: M08 refusal precedence
open_points.text: The answer to an operation the service refuses as a whole. `code` says why
open_points.question: When one request satisfies more than one whole-operation refusal condition, in what order are the conditions checked and which single code wins?
options: Specify one global precedence order
Specify a separate ordered check list for each operation
Permit any applicable refusal code
open_points.default_guess: Specify an ordered check list per operation, beginning with authentication outside M08, then request syntax and safety, project and connection availability, state availability, and operation-specific conflicts.

witness.initial: A delivery request names an unknown project and has a syntactically invalid source_id.
events: The calling flow submits the request.
outcomes: The service returns invalid_source_id because request validation runs first.
The service returns unknown_project because project lookup runs first.

open_points.subject: M08 and authenticated boundary
open_points.text: The answer to an operation the service refuses as a whole. `RefusalCode` is `unknown_project`, `connection_not_confirmed`, `folder_unavailable`, `state_unavailable`, `invalid_source_id`, `unsafe_reference`, `not_placed`, `publication_conflict`.
open_points.question: How is a request with a missing or invalid bearer token represented, given that every operation needs the token but the closed RefusalCode list has no authentication code?
options: Authentication failures are transport-level 401 responses outside M08
Add an authentication RefusalCode member
Map authentication failures to one existing code
open_points.default_guess: Return a transport-level 401 response with a fixed safe body outside the domain M08 model.

witness.initial: The service is running and the request has no valid bearer token.
outcomes: Authentication middleware returns a transport-level 401 without constructing M08.
The operation constructs an M08 refusal using an existing code or an implementation-added authentication code.

open_points.subject: A6 rule 5
open_points.text: the operation is refused with `state_unavailable` and changes nothing.
open_points.rule: Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена (`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note (`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Replace the value-only reference with the emitted member name beside the model address, for example `the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode`.

open_points.subject: INV-20 Required tests
open_points.text: with a damaged placement or mark record, scan, delivery and mark each answer `state_unavailable` and the record stays as it was
open_points.rule: Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена (`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note (`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Name the emitted STATE_UNAVAILABLE member together with `= models.RefusalCode` instead of naming the enum member only by its stored value.
